clinicalPearls: An autosomal recessive combined immunodeficiency caused by loss of coronin-1A, an actin-regulatory protein critical for T-cell survival and migration
The characteristic laboratory finding is T-cell lymphopenia, which may be detected through newborn screening for severe combined immunodeficiency
Presentation ranges from a severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype in infancy to a milder combined immunodeficiency presenting later in childhood
Epstein-Barr-virus-driven lymphoproliferation and B-cell lymphoma are a distinctive complication reflecting impaired T-cell control of the virus
Recurrent respiratory and mucocutaneous infections occur, and some patients have features of immune dysregulation
Diagnosis combines demonstration of reduced naive T cells and impaired T-cell function with confirmatory CORO1A sequencing
Definitive treatment is haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, with immunoglobulin replacement and antimicrobial prophylaxis in the interim
reference.pathophysiology: Coronin-1A, encoded by CORO1A, regulates the actin cytoskeleton and is highly expressed in lymphocytes, where it controls the dynamic actin remodelling needed for thymocyte egress, T-cell survival in the periphery, and T-cell migration and activation. When coronin-1A is deficient, T cells are inefficiently released from the thymus and fail to persist and move normally in the periphery, so naive T-cell numbers fall and T-cell responses are weakened. Because effective control of Epstein-Barr virus depends on cytotoxic T-cell surveillance, this T-cell defect allows the virus to drive B-cell proliferation and predisposes to lymphoproliferative disease and lymphoma. The resulting combined immunodeficiency underlies the susceptibility to recurrent and opportunistic infection.
additionalDifferentials: Typical severe combined immunodeficiency of other genetic causes
Other actin-regulation defects such as DOCK2 and DOCK8 deficiency
X-linked lymphoproliferative disease and other EBV-susceptibility disorders
Ataxia-telangiectasia and other combined immunodeficiencies with lymphopenia
additionalInvestigations: Lymphocyte subset enumeration with naive and memory T-cell analysis
T-cell receptor excision circle quantification, including on newborn screening
Epstein-Barr virus load monitoring and assessment for lymphoproliferation
Quantitative immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
Imaging and histology where lymphoma is suspected
redFlags: Low naive T cells or an abnormal newborn severe combined immunodeficiency screen
Severe or opportunistic infection in infancy
Failure to thrive with recurrent infection
Consanguinity with a family history of early infection or lymphoma
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on severity and on timely recognition; severe infantile disease is life-threatening without haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, and the risk of Epstein-Barr-virus-driven lymphoproliferation adds to morbidity, so early transplantation offers the best outcome.
pitfalls: Overlooking milder later-presenting disease when lymphopenia is only moderate
Attributing lymphoproliferation to primary lymphoma without recognising the underlying immunodeficiency
Giving live vaccines before the T-cell defect is excluded
Missing the diagnosis when newborn screening is unavailable
Delaying transplantation while managing recurrent infections
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the definitive treatment, offering the best outcome and being life-saving in severe infantile combined immunodeficiency
Provide antimicrobial prophylaxis against Pneumocystis, fungal and viral pathogens while immunodeficient
Give immunoglobulin replacement therapy for impaired antibody responses and recurrent infection
Monitor Epstein-Barr virus load and treat virus-driven lymphoproliferation pre-emptively with rituximab, maintaining lymphoma surveillance
Avoid live vaccines and use irradiated, cytomegalovirus-safe blood products
Offer genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive disorder with family testing, and support newborn screening detection through low T-cell receptor excision circles
Manage through a clinical immunology and transplant multidisciplinary team with early referral
